source.title: From Stability to Chaos: Analyzing Gradient Descent Dynamics in Quadratic Regression
source.authors: Xuxing Chen; K. Balasubramanian; Promit Ghosal; Bhavya Agrawalla

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes gradient descent on quadratic regression models and reports how training loss behaves across step-size regimes, using a different model and analysis from the claim’s deep-network benchmark studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for quadratic regression and two-layer quadratic-activation networks, not CIFAR classification. Results cited from other work are not extracted as rows. Figure-only curves are not assigned numerical values.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes constant-step gradient descent under squared loss, proving regimes of nonmonotonic convergence, bounded nonconvergence and divergence in quadratic models, including two-layer quadratic networks. These results bear on V5 through a different model and method; they do not establish its full wide-network or edge-of-stability account.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the main dynamics result but omits the prediction findings. The authors establish five step-size-dependent phases for orthogonal quadratic models, report similar empirical patterns with non-orthogonal data, and propose trajectory averaging to stabilize predictions. Their conclusion claims strongest test accuracy in periodic and chaotic phases, although Section C.2 more specifically reports the best test error roughly in the catapult phase without averaging.
record.recipe_differences: Constant-step-size gradient descent on quadratic regression and two-layer networks with quadratic activation; not the wide-network stability-limit experiments described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with the step-size parameter a: loss converges to zero for 0 < a ≤ 1, remains bounded without converging to zero for 1 < a ≤ 2, and diverges for a > 2. Experiments also vary width, noise variance, and orthogonal versus non-orthogonal data.

fits_no_version.finding: Ergodic trajectory averaging stabilizes predictions and test-loss fluctuations, with test-time cost growing with trajectory length.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Averaging predictions along nonconvergent gradient-descent trajectories can stabilize test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: ReLU network experiments show nonmonotonic, roughly periodic or chaotic patterns, particularly in sharpness plots, without an explicit above-threshold recovery result.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large constant learning rates can produce periodic or chaotic training dynamics in two-layer ReLU networks.

record.problems: Analytical results are for quadratic regression, with the two-layer network characterization relying on orthogonal data. Non-orthogonal and ReLU findings are empirical and shown mainly in plots; the authors state that theoretical characterization there remains future work. The experiments do not quantify the initial linearized-model stability threshold used in V5.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows omitted. Figure-only exact values were not reconstructed from Figures 4 and 6–10.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error, corrupted labels, and SGD or Adam outcomes in sufficiently large convolutional networks.
ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.

Recovery relative to the initial linearized-model stability limit in wide networks; a brief initial loss rise accompanied by curvature reduction; progressive sharpening and sustained hovering at the stability threshold; divergence despite starting below that threshold. The paper's explicit threshold argument uses initial Hessian sharpness in generalized phase retrieval.
Batch normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and normalization-free Fixup training.

missing.what: The study explicitly defines ηcrit = 2/λmax(H0) and considers the proposed catapult interval ηcrit < η < 2ηcrit. For small z0 this corresponds approximately to 1 < a < 2, where its model instead has periodic or chaotic dynamics without zero-loss convergence. This is an argument limiting transfer of a threshold rule, not a direct refutation of V5's original wide-network results.

Theorem 3.3 transfers the cubic-map dynamics and Corollary 1's convergence, bounded-nonconvergence and divergence regimes directly to two-layer quadratic networks with fixed outer weights and orthogonal inputs. Existing analytical rows describe phase retrieval or regression; R6 records only experiments.

Sharpness is analytically linked to the residual: λmax(Ht) = (3zt+2a)/η in the single-sample model, with a maximum over samples in orthogonal regression. In convergent regimes its limit is 2a/η, equaling 2/η at a = 1. This does not establish progressive sharpening or sustained threshold hovering.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Bounded nonconvergence in a different model does not warrant a blanket challenges verdict against V5. Missing threshold measurements and untested widths are not themselves evidence limiting scope.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification, random or corrupted labels, network size, and SGD or Adam training-error outcomes.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual architectures and depth-dependent training error.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, and trainable depth.

The study does not measure the initial linearized-model stability limit, sharpness hovering at a stability threshold, or divergence below that threshold. Its neural-network experiment uses widths 5, 10, and 25 and quadratic activation with fixed outer weights.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training.

rows.subject: Single-data-point generalized phase retrieval model (3.1)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with constant step-size; dynamics characterized by parameter a.
rows.value: Training loss converges to 0; it is monotonic for 0 < a ≤ 2√2 − 2 and has catapults for 2√2 − 2 < a ≤ 1.
rows.note: The paper states that the loss dynamics are captured by the cubic map. The regime is characterized by a, not by an empirically measured stability limit.
rows.check: Split monotonic convergence from catapult convergence. Only 2√2−2 < a ≤ 1 establishes nonmonotonic recovery. The paper's catapult definition permits infinitely recurring increases during convergence, rather than requiring a brief initial rise.

rows.subject: Single-data-point generalized phase retrieval model (3.1)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with constant step-size; dynamics characterized by parameter a.
rows.value: The training dynamics are periodic or chaotic, and the loss does not converge to 0.
rows.note: The paper says periodic or chaotic dynamics occur in this regime; it does not report a numerical loss value.
rows.check: Loss fails to converge to zero; this is absent recovery, not a reversed effect. Bounded periodic or chaotic dynamics are not divergence. The discussion does not establish that this regime lies within V5's recoverable range for wide networks.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, discussion following Theorem 3.1, p. 8; Theorem 2.1, p. 6.

rows.subject: Quadratic regression on multiple orthogonal data points (3.3)
rows.size_stated: n data points; n not fixed in the theorem
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with constant step-size; per-example dynamics governed by ai.
rows.value: Training loss converges to 0; it is decreasing when 0 < max1≤i≤n ai ≤ 2√2 − 2.
rows.note: Analytical result for mutually orthogonal training data.
rows.check: Zero-loss convergence alone does not establish above-threshold recovery. Preserve the assumption that every ai is positive; the maximum alone does not express that assumption. Separate monotonic and nonmonotonic regimes.

rows.subject: Two-layer neural network with quadratic activation and fixed outer-layer weights (3.4)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on hidden-layer weights with constant step-size.
rows.value: Authors state that the curves show the four plotted phases and confirm the theoretical results.
rows.note: The plots show training-loss curves by step-size and noise; no exact curve values are stated in text. The paper says 0.9 and 1 are both in the catapult phase for each m, with 1 the largest step-size allowed in that phase.
rows.check: The values 0.3, 0.9, 1, 1.2 and 1.8 or 1.6 specify max ai, not raw learning rates η. Split the row by phase: convergence with catapults and bounded nonconvergence cannot share one effect state. The text confirms the four phases but does not establish the initial linearized threshold comparison.
